newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Deutsche ends hard year with profit gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Deutsche ends hard year with profit gains.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, on Tuesday reported a 4.8 percent rise in net profit in 1996, a year in which its earnings and image were pummelled by a string of blows including the debacle at Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).

But the bank reported sharply higher-than-expected operating profit after risk provisions which jumped 37 percent to 5.8 billion marks ($3.4 billion). Most analysts had expected a figure closer to five billion marks.

Net income rose to 2.2 billion marks from 2.1 billion marks, trailing behind a 22 percent rise reported by Frankfurt rival Commerzbank AG and lower than an expected 30 percent surge at Germany's Number Two bank, Dresdner Bank AG, which reports its results on Thursday.
Deutsche's shares responded by rising to a three-year high of 87.70 marks in early electronic trade, up 0.60 marks or 0.7 percent from Monday's close.
Deutsche did not provide a breakdown of 1996 earnings but analysts expect its operating profit was in part boosted by gains in trading income fuelled by rallying financial markets.
Full 1996 will be announced at a news conference on March 26.
In a brief statement, Deutsche said its balance sheet total jumped 23 percent to 886 billion marks in 1996 due to increased trading activities as part of its expanding investment banking business.
The loan volume rose by 8.2 percent to 410 billion marks while customer deposits grew by 25 percent to 375 billion marks.

While 1996 is unlikely to have been as bad as for Deutsche as 1994, when it was heavily criticised for its role in the five billion-mark collapse of the Schneider real estate group, the bank suffered its fair share of mishaps last year.

It faces the estimated 200 million-pound cost of compensating investors for alleged mismanagement at three unit trusts run by London-based Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM). The compensation for the affair, which came to light in September, comes on top of a 180 million-pound net injection by Deutsche to shore up the unit trusts.

MGAM followed Deutsche's major contribution to a bail-out of engineering group Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG (KHD) which analysts estimate added more than 200 million marks to the bank's risk provisions for the year.

In addition, two major shareholdings, Daimler-Benz AG and construction group Philipp Holzmann AG, omitted dividends for 1995, costing Deutsche 219 million marks in lost income, according to analysts' estimates.
Analysts said that without more information from the bank it was hard to explain the sharp divergence between stagnant net earnings and buoyant operating profit.
